### Design
- **Selection syntax (D-SB1-1):** no new flag and no new env setting. The existing `--sandbox [mode]` (global, `index.ts:394`, and
  sidecar `:1554`) also accepts a profile:
  `^(auto|bwrap|docker)?(:workspace|:read-only|:network)?$` (at least one part; case-sensitive; ≤ 32 chars), plus the legacy `none`.
  Examples: `--sandbox :workspace`, `--sandbox bwrap:network`. Legacy values keep their exact meaning and set **no** explicit profile.
  Anything else exits 2 listing the valid values. It never falls back to unconfined.
- **New pure module `cli/src/sandbox_profile.ts`:**
  ```ts
  export const SANDBOX_PROFILE_NAMES = [":workspace", ":read-only", ":network"] as const;
  export type SandboxProfileName = typeof SANDBOX_PROFILE_NAMES[number];
  export type ProfileLabel = SandboxProfileName | "unconfined";
  export function parseSandboxValue(raw: string | true | undefined): { engine?: "auto"|"bwrap"|"docker"|"none"; profile?: SandboxProfileName } // throws SandboxProfileError
  export const PROFILE_SPECS: Record<SandboxProfileName, { readOnly: boolean; network: boolean; summary: string; residual: readonly string[] }>;
  export interface SandboxPosture { profile: ProfileLabel; explicit: boolean; engine: "auto"|"bwrap"|"docker"|"none"; network: boolean; readOnly: boolean; source: string; residual: string[] }
  export function describeSandboxPosture(i: { sandbox: boolean|string|undefined; readOnly: boolean; network: boolean; profile?: SandboxProfileName; source?: string }): SandboxPosture
  export function profileRank(p: ProfileLabel): 0|1|2|3; // unconfined < :network < :workspace < :read-only
  ```
- **Mapping (profiles only rename and bundle existing confinement):**

  | Profile | Equals today's flags | Engine | Workspace | HOME | Network |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `:workspace` | `--sandbox [engine]` (default auto), network forced off | bwrap, else docker | rw | tmpfs + toolchain ro mounts | off, even when `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK=1` (warnOnce) |
  | `:network` | `--sandbox [engine] --sandbox-network` | same | rw | same | on |
  | `:read-only` | `--read-only` (`docker:read-only` is refused: read-only confinement is bwrap-only, `tools.ts:1722`) | bwrap | ro (fd-pinned) | tmpfs | off |
  | (none set) | today's behaviour unchanged; the label is derived: readOnly → `:read-only`; sandbox on and network → `:network`; sandbox on → `:workspace`; otherwise `unconfined` | | | | |
- **Composition:**
  - `:read-only` sets `readOnly`, which wins over `--yes`/`--mode auto` exactly as `--read-only` does (`config.ts:466-469`). A tightening.
  - `:workspace` and `:network` leave the approval mode untouched.
  - `--sandbox-network` with `:workspace` or `:read-only` → exit 2 (explicit conflict). With `:network` it is redundant and accepted.
  - Managed policy: `:network` under `sandbox.forbid_network` is refused through `clampSandboxNetwork(policy, true, "--sandbox :network")`.
  - `sandbox.required` with no profile raises the derived label to `:workspace`/`:network` with the policy source (already
    `clampSandbox`).
  - **No new managed policy key** (D-SB1-2): the floor is expressed by the existing keys. A `sandbox.min_profile` key is deferred (it
    would bump the policy `schema_version` while GV-1/GV-5 finish).
- **Network truth:** `sandbox_network.ts` gains `setSandboxNetworkProfile(v: boolean|undefined)`. `sandboxNetworkEnabled()` returns the
  profile value first when set (`sandbox.ts:198`). This closes "the sandbox does not consult the policy" for profiled sessions, because the env
  variable can no longer re-enable network at call time.
- **Config:** `HarnessConfig.sandboxProfile?: SandboxProfileName` (`types.ts`, set only when explicit) and `config.sandbox` as the engine.
- **Visibility:**
  - One describer replaces the three copies (`sidecar.ts:1340`, `doctor.ts:1361`, `repl.ts:380`).
  - `session.state.posture` gains `profile?: string` (additive; schema regen, `VERSIONS.json` entry, samples). Rust `PostureInfo` gains
    `profile: Option<String>`, shown in the TUI posture line.
  - REPL `/status`: `mode: review · sandbox: :workspace (bwrap, network off, explicit) · workspace: trusted`.
  - Doctor: `posture.profile` and `posture.profileSource` (additive; `DOCTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 2, D-SB1-4, because
    `smoke-package.sh` pins 2). The text header prints the same; `sandbox.confinement` evidence adds the profile and its residual list.
  - VR-3: `dispatch_tool_call.ts:677` metadata gains `sandboxProfile: this.sandboxPostureLabel` (one object property, no operator, so the
    complexity is unchanged; the checker confirms it), and `spine.ts:652` passes `profile`.
- **Residual holes**, documented beside each profile in `docs/SANDBOX_PROFILES.md` and in `PROFILE_SPECS.residual`:
  - broad host reads (`/` is bound read-only: `/etc`, `/usr`, other world-readable files);
  - the writable workspace includes `.git` (hooks, config) and ignored trees (`node_modules`), which later host-side tools may execute;
  - toolchain directories are readable;
  - no seccomp filter under bwrap;
  - `:network` is unrestricted egress (no domain filter, separate from the egress inspector);
  - MCP servers and plugins are not sandboxed;
  - the worker falls back to unconfined under `auto` when no engine exists for the **worker**, while commands still refuse
    (`tools.ts:789-831`);
  - `nexus verify --sandbox` does not accept profiles (D-SB1-5).

### Security analysis
A profile is a name for an existing flag bundle and cannot grant:
- No code path reads `sandboxProfile` to decide approval, full access, verification-path mode, CS-9 rules or managed policy.
- `:read-only` only tightens.
- Parsing is strict and fails closed.
- Network can only be turned on by the explicit `:network`, which managed policy can refuse.
- Profile strings never reach a shell: they are parsed against an enum.

G-3 cases below.

## PA-2: verified merge arbitration

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "two units whose changes conflict semantically (each passes alone) fail verification on the merged tree and
neither is integrated silently". Unit text: "when parallel units integrate, apply each diff, run verification on the merged tree, reject
on failure".

### Definitions, from the code
- **Unit:** a `WorkUnit` of a durable operation (`nexus operation run`, `/batch`, `/team`) whose operation has `git.isolate: true`. Only
  then may `maxConcurrentUnits > 1` (`core/operation_schema.ts:~301`; `docs/v1.3.0/PA1_RESOURCE_ADMISSION.md`; `docs/v1.3.0/BATCH.md`).
  Each unit runs in its own worktree and branch from the integration tip (`core/operation_git.ts:1-11`). `/loop` and `/goal` are single
  workspace drivers and produce no merge (`loop.ts`, `goal.ts`), so they are outside PA-2.
- **Merge:** `OperationGit.integrate` (`operation_git.ts:274-428`): commit the unit's worktree; `git merge --no-ff --no-verify` the unit
  branch into `nexus/op-<key>/integration` in the integration worktree (`:388-397`); on a textual conflict, abort and return `conflict`
  (`:392-397`). Integration is **serialized** by `OperationRunner.enqueueIntegration` (`core/operation_runner.ts:485-506`).
  `integrateUnit` (`:512-580`) turns `conflict` and `failed` into operator decisions (`MERGE_CONFLICT`, `INTEGRATION_FAILED`) and
  `integrated` into a receipt (`IntegrationReceipt`, `core/operation.ts:351-367`) plus `WORK_INTEGRATED`.
- **Verification on the merged tree today:** `verifyMerged(command)` (`operation_git.ts:627-646`, `runVerifierShell` in the integration
  worktree) re-runs **only the integrating unit's own verifier**, and only if that verifier PASSED with executed tests (`:400-402`). A
  failure resets the merge (`:404-409`, `restoreIntegration`). Without a verifier the receipt says `NOT_RUN` and the unit is integrated
  "(not re-verified)" (`operation_runner.ts:565-571`). The crash path re-checks after the fact (`:345-379`). Existing test:
  `cli/test/operation_git.test.ts:170-194`.
- **The gap that fails the acceptance:** with units A and B, B integrated first and passing, then A merging cleanly, A's own narrow verifier
  passes on the merged tree, **B's verifier is never re-run**, and A is integrated even though B's tests now fail. That is the silent
  semantic conflict.

### Design
- **Merged-tree check set** (`integrationChecks()` in `operation_git.ts`), ordered and de-duplicated by exact command string, with owners
  merged:
  1. the operator's verifiers pinned for the operation: `OperationGitState.integrationVerifiers?: string[]`, set at the first run from
     `config.authoritativeVerifierCommand` and unioned with the current one on resume (tighten-only);
  2. the integrating unit's own verifier (as today: PASSED with executed tests);
  3. every earlier receipt's `tests.command` with `status === "PASSED" && hasExecutedTests`, in `sequence` order.

  At most **16** distinct commands (D-PA2-3). Beyond that the integration is `failed` ("too many distinct verifiers; give the operation an
  `--authoritative-verifier`").
- **Run:** sequentially on the merged tip in the integration worktree with the existing per-command timeout; stop at the first failure.
- **Attribution:** on failure, `restoreIntegration(tip)` (as today), then re-run **only the failing check** on the pre-merge tip.
  - It passes there → **semantic conflict**: `failed` with reason "merging <A> breaks the verifier of <owners> (`cmd`) on the merged tree;
    it passes without <A>", `conflictWith: owners`.
  - It fails there too → "the integration branch already fails `cmd` before <A> was merged (environment or unstable verifier); not
    attributed to <A>".
  - Exit 126/127 keeps today's environment message.
- **Verification-file takeover (hostile):** if the merge diff (`tip..mergedTip`) modifies a path that is (a) in an earlier receipt's
  `files` and (b) a verification path by `SecurityManager`'s classifier (`security.ts`, `VERIFICATION_CONFIG_PROTECTED` and the
  verification-path patterns), the merge is reset and `failed` with "<A> changes verification files integrated by <B>: …", before any
  check runs. Without this, A could weaken B's test and pass B's check.
- **Shapes (additive):**
  `interface MergedCheck { command: string; owners: string[] /* unit ids or "operator" */; status: "PASSED"|"FAILED"|"ENVIRONMENT"|"TIMED_OUT"; baseline?: "PASSED"|"FAILED" }`.
  `IntegrationReceipt.mergedChecks?: MergedCheck[]`. `IntegrateResult` `failed` gains `checks?: MergedCheck[]; conflictWith?: string[]`.
  New `OperationEventType` `"INTEGRATION_REJECTED"` with `detail: { unitId, conflictWith, checks }`. Block cause stays
  `INTEGRATION_FAILED`. The question names both units, with options `retry` (re-run the unit with the reason) and `revise`. The existing
  `verification` field values keep their meaning.
- **Crash path** (`:345-379`): uses the same set, and keeps today's "merge already in place" handling on failure.
- **Empty set** (no operator verifier, no unit verifier, no earlier verifiers): `NOT_RUN`, as today, with the same event. This is not
  silent, because the receipt and the event say "not re-verified".
- **Interpretation of "neither is integrated silently" (D-PA2-1):** integration is serialized, so the first unit integrates with a
  verified receipt. The second is refused with an `INTEGRATION_REJECTED` event and a blocking decision that names both units. No unit is
  integrated without a recorded check result, and none is integrated after failing one.
- **Operation schema** 4 → **5** (D-PA2-4): v4 records migrate unchanged. Older builds refuse v5, so an operation started on v1.3.0 cannot
  be resumed by a v1.2.x build that would skip the cumulative checks. Coordinate with Codex lanes on `operation_schema.ts` and its tests:
  only one bump per release window. Rebase onto theirs if they bump first, and fold this into the same version.

### Security analysis
- Merged checks run host-side, unsandboxed, in the integration worktree, as `verifyMerged` does today. Earlier units' verifier commands
  are the same commands that already ran there at their own integration, so trust does not widen. Sandboxing integration checks (reusing
  VR-1's verify sandbox) is a documented follow-up.
- A unit cannot weaken another unit's test and pass: that is the verification-file rule above.
- A unit's own `true`-style verifier cannot mask an earlier failing check, because all checks run.
- An operator verifier is never dropped on resume (union).
- The integration worktree is restored on every failure path. A failed restore blocks the operation (`blockOnGit`, `operation_runner.ts:656-668`).
- No path marks a unit VERIFIED from integration, and the turn-level outcome ladder is untouched.

## PF-3: transport beyond a parent's stdio (unix socket, token, attach and reattach)

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "a second client attaches to a running session; a wrong token is refused; the socket is mode 0600".
Unit text: "a unix domain socket (default) with a token and origin check for any localhost HTTP/WebSocket listener (reference: goose
`acp/transport/auth.rs`, constant-time compare); several clients may attach and reattach".

### What exists (read)

  negotiation, which is per connection: `negotiated` (`:148`), and `initialize` (`:315-331`) refuses a second `initialize` with BAD_REQUEST.
- Approvals: `requestApproval`/`openApproval` queue one at a time and emit `approval.request` with id `approval-N` (`:860-891`).
  `resolveApproval` with `always: true` sets `alwaysApprove`, switches the mode to `auto` and re-emits `session.state` (`:893-908`, grant at
  `:899-904`). So today any writer to the sidecar's stdin can grant allow-always.
- `hello` and the first `session.state` are emitted once, in `start()` (`:170-196`). `emitSessionState` is private (`:1335-1360`).
- Process entry `main` (`:1529-1625`): its own commander, the client lease, pending-restore recovery, `buildConfig`, and stdin through
  `readline` with **no line cap** (`:1615-1618`, and `docs/PROTOCOL.md` ~`:42` "sets no limit on the length of a line it reads"). EOF
  on stdin means shutdown (`:1619-1623`). Guarded by `isEntryPoint` (`:1628-1643`).
- Protocol: `PROTOCOL_VERSION=1`, range `:13-22`, `SIDECAR_CAPABILITIES` `:34-55`, `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES=[]` `:62`, `ErrorCode` `:76`,
  `SidecarCommand` `:257-288`, `parseCommand` `:305`. Schema `docs/protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json` + ledger `docs/protocol/VERSIONS.json`
  (additive changes keep protocol 1 with a note, `docs/protocol/README.md` "Recording a version decision"). `docs/PROTOCOL.md:9-15` states
  "No socket or network transport ... (planned as PF-3)".
- Reusable pieces: `BoundedLineReader` (`cli/src/acp/jsonrpc.ts:34-103`, cap and oversized reporting), `ACP_MAX_LINE_BYTES=4 MiB` and
  `ACP_MAX_OVERSIZED_LINES=3` (`acp/types.ts:97-99`), `ACP_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS=600` (`acp/types.ts:120`), and the ACP refusal of auto
  approval at startup (`index.ts:1526-1539`, `acpStartupRefusal`). The private-dir and `lstat` pattern is in `core/client_lease.ts`
  (`clientLeasePath`: `/tmp/nexus-client-leases-<uid>`, 0700, lstat-checked), and `writePrivateFile` is in `core/durable_file.ts:120`.
- Sandbox already hides `/run/user/<uid>` from write-mode bwrap commands (`--tmpfs`, `cli/src/sandbox.ts:804-806`), and `/tmp` is a
  fresh tmpfs in both bwrap branches. The read-only branch starts from `--tmpfs /` (`:741-770`). Docker mounts only the workspace.
- XERJ (goose, lexical): `crates/goose/src/acp/transport/mod.rs:184-223` uses an `x-secret-key` header with an `AcpOriginPolicy`,
  but its aux routes use `CorsLayer::allow_origin(Any)`. We take the shared-secret idea and reject any HTTP listener.

### Design
**Scope decision (D-PF3-1):** v1.3.0 ships **a unix domain socket only, with no TCP, HTTP or WebSocket listener**. The unit asks for an origin check
only "for any localhost HTTP/WebSocket listener", so with no such listener there is nothing to check. The acceptance names only the
socket, the token and mode 0600, so it is met in full. A browser cannot open an `AF_UNIX` connection, so DNS rebinding and CSRF have no
way in. A guard test keeps a port from appearing.

**Command:** `nexus serve` (new file `cli/src/serve_cli.ts`, `registerServeCommand(program)`; `index.ts` gains 2 lines beside
`registerOperationCommands`, `:1542`). It takes the global options (endpoint, model, `-w`, `--sandbox`, `--authoritative-verifier`, ...) as
`acp` does (`index.ts:1529`). Its own options are `--idle-timeout <secs>` (default 1800; 0 means never) and `--session <id>` (resume, as the
sidecar's `-r`). It refuses to start, with exit 2:
- under auto approval (`-y`, `--mode auto`, `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto`), reusing `acpStartupRefusal`;
- when commands would run unconfined (D-PF3-6): the effective sandbox profile must be `:workspace`, `:network` or `:read-only` (SB-1's
  `describeSandboxPosture`). With no `--sandbox`, `serve` defaults to `:workspace`. `--sandbox none` is refused. Before SB-1 lands, use
  `sandbox: "auto"` and refuse `none`.

Stdout prints exactly one line, `{"v":1,"type":"listening","socket":"<path>","descriptor":"<path>","pid":N,"experimental":true}`, and nothing
else; diagnostics go to stderr. The **token is never printed**.

**Runtime directory** (`socketRuntimeDir(env, uid)` in a new `cli/src/session_socket.ts`):
1. `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nexus` when `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is absolute and `lstat` shows a real directory owned by the euid with `mode & 0o077 === 0`.
2. Otherwise `/tmp/nexus-sockets-<uid>`, created 0700 and lstat-checked exactly as `clientLeasePath` does (not a symlink, owned by
   the euid, no group/other bits). Fail closed with a message naming the path.
3. The `nexus` subdir is created 0700. A pre-existing one is accepted only if it passes the same checks.

**Files per server** (`s-<16 hex>` from `randomBytes(8)`, so every path is well under the 108-byte `sun_path` limit):
- `s-<hex>.sock`: `server.listen({ path })`, then `fs.chmodSync(path, 0o600)` before the descriptor is written. The 0700 directory means no
  other uid can connect even in the window before the chmod.
- `s-<hex>.json` (`writePrivateFile`, 0600, atomic), format `nexus-socket/1`:
  `{"format":"nexus-socket/1","socket":"<abs>","token":"<64 lowercase hex>","pid":N,"session":"<session id>","workspace":"<abs>","started_at":"<ISO>","protocol_min":1,"protocol_max":1,"experimental":true}`.
  The token is 32 bytes from `crypto.randomBytes`, new for every server start.
- On exit (shutdown, SIGTERM, SIGINT, idle timeout) the socket and the descriptor are unlinked. At start, a sweep deletes `s-*.json`
  and `.sock` pairs whose `pid` is gone (`kill(pid,0)` → ESRCH) **and** whose socket refuses a connection (ECONNREFUSED). Any other state
  is left alone and logged.

**Wire format:** the same NDJSON as stdio, read with `BoundedLineReader`. The cap is 4 KiB before attach and 4 MiB
(`SOCKET_MAX_LINE_BYTES`, new in `protocol.ts`) after it. Each oversized line gets BAD_REQUEST, and the third one closes the connection.

Attach handshake: within 5 s of connecting, the first line must be:
```
{"v":1,"type":"attach","id":"<id>","token":"<64 hex>","role":"control"|"observe","client":{"name":"...","version":"..."}}
```
- Success: `{"v":1,"type":"attached","id":"<id>","connection":"c<N>","role":"control"|"observe","session":"<id>","experimental":true}`,
  then this connection alone gets the current `hello` and `session.state`. A controller also gets the pending `approval.request`, re-sent
  with the **same id**, if one is open.
- Any failure (bad, missing or short token, malformed attach, attach not first, timeout) gets one identical
  `{"type":"error","id":<id or absent>,"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"attach refused"}`, then the socket ends. The message does not say why.
  The comparison is `timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, after `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`.
- A `role: "control"` request while a controller is attached gets `BUSY` ("another client controls this session"). There is no takeover.
- Over 8 connections gets `BUSY` and close.
- `attach` sent on stdio gets BAD_REQUEST ("attach is only used on a socket connection").

Protocol additions (additive, so protocol stays 1, with a `VERSIONS.json` entry): `attach` in `SidecarCommand`; `attached` in
`SidecarEvent`; `ErrorCode += "UNAUTHORIZED" | "NOT_CONTROLLER" | "NOT_PERMITTED"`; the constant `SOCKET_MAX_LINE_BYTES`. The Rust TUI
does not use the socket. Its event parser ignores unknown event types, so the Rust change is limited to regenerating the samples
(`cli/test/fixtures/protocol_v1_schema_samples.jsonl`).

**Multi-client model (hub = `SessionSocketServer` in `session_socket.ts`):** one `SidecarServer` per `nexus serve` process. Its `write`
**broadcasts** each already-formatted line to every attached connection; no ids are rewritten.
- **Controller** (at most one): may send `prompt.submit`, `steer`, `cancel`, `approve` (once only), `deny`, `answer`, `checkpoint.choice`,
  `receipt`, `tool.detail`, `models.list`, `model.select`, `shutdown`, and `slash` where `readOnlySlashAllowed(command,args)` (`sidecar.ts:38-49`)
  holds and the command is not `mode auto`, plus `slash compact`.
- **Not permitted over the socket** (`NOT_PERMITTED`, sent to the sender only, nothing forwarded): `approve` with `always:true`, which the hub
  downgrades to `always:false` and answers with a `notice` to the controller: "allow-always is not available over the socket; approved once".
  Also refused: `slash mode auto`, `!<cmd>`, `/cd`, any other slash outside the allowlist, and `provider.connect|cancel|local-cancel|disconnect`.
  Rule: **a socket client can drive turns and give one human yes or no per approval. It cannot raise the session's authority or change
  Nexus configuration** (D-PF3-4).
- **Observer:** may send only `initialize` and nothing else (`NOT_CONTROLLER` to that observer only). It sees the full stream, including
  `approval.request` and responses to the controller's requests.
- `initialize` is answered **by the hub, per connection**, through a pure `negotiate(clientMin, clientMax, experimental, offered)` extracted
  from `SidecarServer.initialize` (`:315-331`; behaviour-preserving, and `SidecarServer.initialize` calls it). It is never forwarded, so the
  server's `negotiated` stays unset. `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES` is empty today, so experimental sidecar features are simply unavailable over the socket.
- **Reattach:** when the controller disconnects, a pending approval **stays pending** and the turn keeps running. The next connection that
  attaches as `control` receives the re-sent `approval.request` and may answer it. An approval with no controller attached for 600 s
  (`ACP_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS`) is **denied** (`resolveApproval(id,false,false)`, which never grants), with a notice. There is no replay of
  events from before an attach (D-PF3-8): an attacher gets current state, and can fetch `receipt` afterwards.
- **Lifecycle:** the server exits on the controller's `shutdown`, on SIGTERM or SIGINT, or on idle timeout. Idle means zero connections
  and no turn running for `--idle-timeout`. EOF from one client is a detach and never a shutdown.
- **Backpressure:** a connection whose `socket.writableLength` exceeds 8 MiB is destroyed (logged on stderr). A slow observer cannot stall
  the session or other clients.

`SidecarServer` changes (small, behaviour-preserving for stdio):
- `public helloEvent()` and `public sessionStateEvent()`, extracted from `start()` and `emitSessionState()`.
- `public pendingApprovalEvent(): SidecarEvent | undefined`: `openApproval` keeps the event object it emitted on `pendingApproval`.
- `public answerApprovalForTimeout(id)`, or reuse `resolveApproval(id,false,false)` through a public `deny(id)`.
- `negotiate()` extracted.
None of these runs in the stdio path differently. The wire recordings (`cli/test/fixtures/wire/*.json`, `protocol_wire.test.ts`) must replay
unchanged.

**Library side** (with PF-4): `attachSidecar({ descriptor | socket+token, role })` in `cli/src/sidecar_client.ts` returns the same
`SidecarClient` over a `net.Socket`. It reads the descriptor itself (`lstat` + regular file + 0600 + owner = euid, ≤ 4 KiB).

### Security analysis
- **Who can connect:** only processes with the same uid (and root). The 0700 directory plus the 0600 socket means `connect()` needs search
  permission on the directory and write permission on the socket. Node cannot read `SO_PEERCRED` without a native addon, so peer uid is not
  checked; that is documented.
- **What the token protects against:** (1) a process that can reach the socket path but cannot read the descriptor (a sandbox that
  bind-mounts a path, or a widened directory mode); (2) attaching to the wrong server when a path or descriptor is stale or mixed up;
  (3) accidental attach by same-uid tools that walk sockets. **It does not protect against unconfined code running as the user**, which can
  read the descriptor. That is why `serve` requires confined commands (D-PF3-6): a model-driven `run_command` in bwrap sees a tmpfs at
  `/run/user/<uid>` and `/tmp`. Slice 2 adds an explicit `--tmpfs <socket dir>` to both bwrap branches and the worker wrap, so a
  non-standard `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is masked too. Docker never mounts it. Residual hole, documented: unsandboxed MCP servers and plugins, and
  any host process of the user, can read the token and attach as observer, or as controller when none is attached.
- **A second client cannot answer the first client's approval:** only the single controller connection may approve or deny. An observer gets
  `NOT_CONTROLLER` and the approval stays pending. The answer comes from a human through a client, and the gate decided first
  (`docs/PROTOCOL.md:17`). A forged `approve` for a refused action cannot reach a gate the sidecar already refused, because no
  `approval.request` exists for it (`NO_PENDING_APPROVAL`).
- **No grant over the socket:** no allow-always, no `/mode auto`, no `!` shell, no `/cd`, and no credential writes. Managed policy is
  unchanged: the sidecar config was clamped at `buildConfig`.
- **DoS bounds:** at most 8 connections, a 4 KiB pre-auth line, a 5 s attach deadline, 4 MiB lines, three oversized lines then close, and
  8 MiB of outbound buffer per connection.
- The token never appears in logs, stdout, events, errors or the flight log. `formatSafeSidecarEvent` never sees commands.

## PF-4: library entry point

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "an example script runs a verified task through the entry point in CI". Unit text: "a `lib` entry that does not
run commander on import, `exports` and `types` in `cli/package.json`, a package name decision, a documented minimal embedding example that
spawns the sidecar".

### What exists
- `cli/package.json`: `"name":"local-code-harness"`, `"main":"dist/index.js"`, `"bin":{"harness":"./dist/index.js"}`, `"license":"MIT"`; no
  `exports`, `types` or `private`.
- `cli/tsconfig.json`: no `declaration`.
- `cli/src/index.ts` is the CLI. Importing it runs top-level code: `isolateEvalCommandHome`, the client lease, restore recovery,
  `loadEnvironment()` and possible `process.exit(2)` (`:70-134`), then `await program.parseAsync(process.argv)` (`:1565`). It re-exports
  `ApplicationCore` after that (`:1567-1568`, the "accidental re-export" of PLAN §2). The managed-policy startup check is in the `preAction`
  hook (`:1545-1563`).
- The sidecar is a process: `cli/src/sidecar.ts` `main`, guarded by `isEntryPoint` (`:1628-1643`). The CLI finds it with
  `resolveSidecarScript` (`index.ts:193-213`) and the TUI is launched with `--sidecar <script> --node <execPath>` (`:215-227`).
- Out-of-process is the safe embedding. In-process `ApplicationCore` (`core/app.ts:88-102`) would bypass the client lease,
  pending-restore recovery and `requireManagedPolicyAtStartup`, all of which `sidecar.ts main` (`:1589-1601`) and `index.ts` perform.
- A verified run recipe exists: `cli/test/run_json_contract.test.ts:218-251` (`FIXABLE_PROJECT`, `FIX_REPLIES`, `--deliverable-file math.js`
  → `turn.outcome === "VERIFIED"`). `examples/verified-completion/` does the same through the CLI.
- Packaging: `scripts/package-linux.sh:35-36` builds, `:64-66` copies all of `cli/dist` plus `package.json`/lock and runs
  `npm ci --omit=dev`. The CI repro job builds twice and `cmp`s the tarball, sums, notices, SBOM and installer (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:327-334`,
  `release.yml:109-116`). `scripts/smoke-package.sh` smoke-tests the extracted tarball. CI builds `cli` before tests (`ci.yml:153-154`).
- No repository code resolves the package by name (`git grep local-code-harness` finds only an evidence doc).

### Design
- **New `cli/src/lib.ts`** (the only `exports` target). Its runtime import graph is limited to `sidecar_client.ts`, `acp/jsonrpc.ts`
  (`BoundedLineReader`) and node builtins. Everything else is `export type`.
  ```ts
  export const NEXUS_LIB_API_VERSION = 1;
  export { spawnSidecar, SidecarClient, SidecarClientError } from "./sidecar_client.js";
  export type { SpawnSidecarOptions, PromptOptions, ApprovalHandler, ApprovalDecision } from "./sidecar_client.js";
  export type { SidecarEvent, SidecarCommand, ErrorCode } from "./protocol.js";
  export type { TurnResult, EngineeringOutcome, ExecutionState } from "./core/turn.js";
  ```
  PF-3 adds `attachSidecar`.
- **New `cli/src/sidecar_client.ts`:**
  - `spawnSidecar(opts): Promise<SidecarClient>`, where
    `SpawnSidecarOptions = { workspace: string; endpoint?; model?; mode?: "review"|"read-only"; authoritativeVerifier?; deliverableFiles?: string[]; sandbox?: string; extraArgs?: readonly string[]; env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv; node?: string; sidecarScript?: string; signal?: AbortSignal; readyTimeoutMs?: number /*30_000*/ }`.
  - Defaults: `node = process.execPath`; `sidecarScript = new URL("./sidecar" + (import.meta.url.endsWith(".ts") ? ".ts" : ".js"), import.meta.url)`,
    with `--import tsx` added only in the `.ts` case (the VR-2 worker precedent). The lib reads **no** env, HOME or argv itself; the child
    does, as the TUI's child does.
  - Spawn: `spawn(node, [script, "-w", ws, ...flags, ...extraArgs], { stdio: ["pipe","pipe","pipe"], env })`.
  - stdout goes through `BoundedLineReader(16 MiB = ACP_MAX_CHILD_LINE_BYTES)`. A non-JSON or oversized line becomes a `protocol-error`
    client event and never a crash. stderr keeps its last 64 KiB as `client.stderrTail` and is never echoed.
  - `SidecarClient` methods:
    - `hello` (resolved before `spawnSidecar` resolves);
    - `initialize({name,version}) → initialized`;
    - `prompt(text, { onApproval?, signal? }) → Promise<turn.result event>`. One at a time; a second call rejects `BUSY`. The id is
      `lib-<n>`. It resolves on `turn.result` with `turn_id === id`, rejects on `error` with that id, and rejects on child exit.
    - `onApproval(req) → "approve"|"deny"`. The **default denies**. The client sends `{"type":"approve","id","always":false}` and **never
      sends `always:true`**: there is no API for it (D-PF4-3).
    - `receipt()`, `cancel()`, `on("event"|"exit"|"protocol-error")`.
    - `shutdown({graceMs=10_000})`: send `shutdown`, end stdin, wait; then SIGTERM, and SIGKILL after 5 s, **to `child.pid` only**.
      Resolves `{code, signal}`.
- **`cli/package.json`:** `"main":"dist/lib.js"`, `"types":"dist/types/lib.d.ts"`,
  `"exports":{".":{"types":"./dist/types/lib.d.ts","import":"./dist/lib.js"},"./package.json":"./package.json"}`, `"private": true`
  (D13: not published; `npm publish` then fails). `bin` is unchanged. Build script becomes
  `tsc && tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json && node scripts/copy_data.mjs && node scripts/write_build_info.mjs`.

## SB-1: named permission profiles

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "CLI and doctor show the effective profile; a profile cannot disable verification-path protection, grant
allow-always, or bypass G-3; existing sandbox tests pass under profile aliases; residual holes are documented beside the profile".
D22 default taken: ship `:workspace`, `:read-only`, `:network`. The interactive default stays today's engine defaults until a profile is set
explicitly. Managed policy may force a stricter profile, never a looser one.

### Design
- **Selection syntax (D-SB1-1):** no new flag and no new env setting. The existing `--sandbox [mode]` (global, `index.ts:394`, and
  sidecar `:1554`) also accepts a profile:
  `^(auto|bwrap|docker)?(:workspace|:read-only|:network)?$` (at least one part; case-sensitive; ≤ 32 chars), plus the legacy `none`.
  Examples: `--sandbox :workspace`, `--sandbox bwrap:network`. Legacy values keep their exact meaning and set **no** explicit profile.
  Anything else exits 2 listing the valid values. It never falls back to unconfined.
- **New pure module `cli/src/sandbox_profile.ts`:**
  ```ts
  export const SANDBOX_PROFILE_NAMES = [":workspace", ":read-only", ":network"] as const;
  export type SandboxProfileName = typeof SANDBOX_PROFILE_NAMES[number];
  export type ProfileLabel = SandboxProfileName | "unconfined";
  export function parseSandboxValue(raw: string | true | undefined): { engine?: "auto"|"bwrap"|"docker"|"none"; profile?: SandboxProfileName } // throws SandboxProfileError
  export const PROFILE_SPECS: Record<SandboxProfileName, { readOnly: boolean; network: boolean; summary: string; residual: readonly string[] }>;
  export interface SandboxPosture { profile: ProfileLabel; explicit: boolean; engine: "auto"|"bwrap"|"docker"|"none"; network: boolean; readOnly: boolean; source: string; residual: string[] }
  export function describeSandboxPosture(i: { sandbox: boolean|string|undefined; readOnly: boolean; network: boolean; profile?: SandboxProfileName; source?: string }): SandboxPosture
  export function profileRank(p: ProfileLabel): 0|1|2|3; // unconfined < :network < :workspace < :read-only
  ```
- **Mapping (profiles only rename and bundle existing confinement):**

  | Profile | Equals today's flags | Engine | Workspace | HOME | Network |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `:workspace` | `--sandbox [engine]` (default auto), network forced off | bwrap, else docker | rw | tmpfs + toolchain ro mounts | off, even when `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK=1` (warnOnce) |
  | `:network` | `--sandbox [engine] --sandbox-network` | same | rw | same | on |
  | `:read-only` | `--read-only` (`docker:read-only` is refused: read-only confinement is bwrap-only, `tools.ts:1722`) | bwrap | ro (fd-pinned) | tmpfs | off |
  | (none set) | today's behaviour unchanged; the label is derived: readOnly → `:read-only`; sandbox on and network → `:network`; sandbox on → `:workspace`; otherwise `unconfined` | | | | |
- **Composition:**
  - `:read-only` sets `readOnly`, which wins over `--yes`/`--mode auto` exactly as `--read-only` does (`config.ts:466-469`). A tightening.
  - `:workspace` and `:network` leave the approval mode untouched.
  - `--sandbox-network` with `:workspace` or `:read-only` → exit 2 (explicit conflict). With `:network` it is redundant and accepted.
  - Managed policy: `:network` under `sandbox.forbid_network` is refused through `clampSandboxNetwork(policy, true, "--sandbox :network")`.
  - `sandbox.required` with no profile raises the derived label to `:workspace`/`:network` with the policy source (already
    `clampSandbox`).
  - **No new managed policy key** (D-SB1-2): the floor is expressed by the existing keys. A `sandbox.min_profile` key is deferred (it
    would bump the policy `schema_version` while GV-1/GV-5 finish).
- **Network truth:** `sandbox_network.ts` gains `setSandboxNetworkProfile(v: boolean|undefined)`. `sandboxNetworkEnabled()` returns the
  profile value first when set (`sandbox.ts:198`). This closes "the sandbox does not consult the policy" for profiled sessions, because the env
  variable can no longer re-enable network at call time.
- **Config:** `HarnessConfig.sandboxProfile?: SandboxProfileName` (`types.ts`, set only when explicit) and `config.sandbox` as the engine.
- **Visibility:**
  - One describer replaces the three copies (`sidecar.ts:1340`, `doctor.ts:1361`, `repl.ts:380`).
  - `session.state.posture` gains `profile?: string` (additive; schema regen, `VERSIONS.json` entry, samples). Rust `PostureInfo` gains
    `profile: Option<String>`, shown in the TUI posture line.
  - REPL `/status`: `mode: review · sandbox: :workspace (bwrap, network off, explicit) · workspace: trusted`.
  - Doctor: `posture.profile` and `posture.profileSource` (additive; `DOCTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 2, D-SB1-4, because
    `smoke-package.sh` pins 2). The text header prints the same; `sandbox.confinement` evidence adds the profile and its residual list.
  - VR-3: `dispatch_tool_call.ts:677` metadata gains `sandboxProfile: this.sandboxPostureLabel` (one object property, no operator, so the
    complexity is unchanged; the checker confirms it), and `spine.ts:652` passes `profile`.
- **Residual holes**, documented beside each profile in `docs/SANDBOX_PROFILES.md` and in `PROFILE_SPECS.residual`:
  - broad host reads (`/` is bound read-only: `/etc`, `/usr`, other world-readable files);
  - the writable workspace includes `.git` (hooks, config) and ignored trees (`node_modules`), which later host-side tools may execute;
  - toolchain directories are readable;
  - no seccomp filter under bwrap;
  - `:network` is unrestricted egress (no domain filter, separate from the egress inspector);
  - MCP servers and plugins are not sandboxed;
  - the worker falls back to unconfined under `auto` when no engine exists for the **worker**, while commands still refuse
    (`tools.ts:789-831`);
  - `nexus verify --sandbox` does not accept profiles (D-SB1-5).

### Security analysis
A profile is a name for an existing flag bundle and cannot grant:
- No code path reads `sandboxProfile` to decide approval, full access, verification-path mode, CS-9 rules or managed policy.
- `:read-only` only tightens.
- Parsing is strict and fails closed.
- Network can only be turned on by the explicit `:network`, which managed policy can refuse.
- Profile strings never reach a shell: they are parsed against an enum.

G-3 cases below.

## PA-2: verified merge arbitration

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "two units whose changes conflict semantically (each passes alone) fail verification on the merged tree and
neither is integrated silently". Unit text: "when parallel units integrate, apply each diff, run verification on the merged tree, reject
on failure".

### Definitions, from the code
- **Unit:** a `WorkUnit` of a durable operation (`nexus operation run`, `/batch`, `/team`) whose operation has `git.isolate: true`. Only
  then may `maxConcurrentUnits > 1` (`core/operation_schema.ts:~301`; `docs/v1.3.0/PA1_RESOURCE_ADMISSION.md`; `docs/v1.3.0/BATCH.md`).
  Each unit runs in its own worktree and branch from the integration tip (`core/operation_git.ts:1-11`). `/loop` and `/goal` are single
  workspace drivers and produce no merge (`loop.ts`, `goal.ts`), so they are outside PA-2.
- **Merge:** `OperationGit.integrate` (`operation_git.ts:274-428`): commit the unit's worktree; `git merge --no-ff --no-verify` the unit
  branch into `nexus/op-<key>/integration` in the integration worktree (`:388-397`); on a textual conflict, abort and return `conflict`
  (`:392-397`). Integration is **serialized** by `OperationRunner.enqueueIntegration` (`core/operation_runner.ts:485-506`).
  `integrateUnit` (`:512-580`) turns `conflict` and `failed` into operator decisions (`MERGE_CONFLICT`, `INTEGRATION_FAILED`) and
  `integrated` into a receipt (`IntegrationReceipt`, `core/operation.ts:351-367`) plus `WORK_INTEGRATED`.
- **Verification on the merged tree today:** `verifyMerged(command)` (`operation_git.ts:627-646`, `runVerifierShell` in the integration
  worktree) re-runs **only the integrating unit's own verifier**, and only if that verifier PASSED with executed tests (`:400-402`). A
  failure resets the merge (`:404-409`, `restoreIntegration`). Without a verifier the receipt says `NOT_RUN` and the unit is integrated
  "(not re-verified)" (`operation_runner.ts:565-571`). The crash path re-checks after the fact (`:345-379`). Existing test:
  `cli/test/operation_git.test.ts:170-194`.
- **The gap that fails the acceptance:** with units A and B, B integrated first and passing, then A merging cleanly, A's own narrow verifier
  passes on the merged tree, **B's verifier is never re-run**, and A is integrated even though B's tests now fail. That is the silent
  semantic conflict.

### Design
- **Merged-tree check set** (`integrationChecks()` in `operation_git.ts`), ordered and de-duplicated by exact command string, with owners
  merged:
  1. the operator's verifiers pinned for the operation: `OperationGitState.integrationVerifiers?: string[]`, set at the first run from
     `config.authoritativeVerifierCommand` and unioned with the current one on resume (tighten-only);
  2. the integrating unit's own verifier (as today: PASSED with executed tests);
  3. every earlier receipt's `tests.command` with `status === "PASSED" && hasExecutedTests`, in `sequence` order.

  At most **16** distinct commands (D-PA2-3). Beyond that the integration is `failed` ("too many distinct verifiers; give the operation an
  `--authoritative-verifier`").
- **Run:** sequentially on the merged tip in the integration worktree with the existing per-command timeout; stop at the first failure.
- **Attribution:** on failure, `restoreIntegration(tip)` (as today), then re-run **only the failing check** on the pre-merge tip.
  - It passes there → **semantic conflict**: `failed` with reason "merging <A> breaks the verifier of <owners> (`cmd`) on the merged tree;
    it passes without <A>", `conflictWith: owners`.
  - It fails there too → "the integration branch already fails `cmd` before <A> was merged (environment or unstable verifier); not
    attributed to <A>".
  - Exit 126/127 keeps today's environment message.
- **Verification-file takeover (hostile):** if the merge diff (`tip..mergedTip`) modifies a path that is (a) in an earlier receipt's
  `files` and (b) a verification path by `SecurityManager`'s classifier (`security.ts`, `VERIFICATION_CONFIG_PROTECTED` and the
  verification-path patterns), the merge is reset and `failed` with "<A> changes verification files integrated by <B>: …", before any
  check runs. Without this, A could weaken B's test and pass B's check.
- **Shapes (additive):**
  `interface MergedCheck { command: string; owners: string[] /* unit ids or "operator" */; status: "PASSED"|"FAILED"|"ENVIRONMENT"|"TIMED_OUT"; baseline?: "PASSED"|"FAILED" }`.
  `IntegrationReceipt.mergedChecks?: MergedCheck[]`. `IntegrateResult` `failed` gains `checks?: MergedCheck[]; conflictWith?: string[]`.
  New `OperationEventType` `"INTEGRATION_REJECTED"` with `detail: { unitId, conflictWith, checks }`. Block cause stays
  `INTEGRATION_FAILED`. The question names both units, with options `retry` (re-run the unit with the reason) and `revise`. The existing
  `verification` field values keep their meaning.
- **Crash path** (`:345-379`): uses the same set, and keeps today's "merge already in place" handling on failure.
- **Empty set** (no operator verifier, no unit verifier, no earlier verifiers): `NOT_RUN`, as today, with the same event. This is not
  silent, because the receipt and the event say "not re-verified".
- **Interpretation of "neither is integrated silently" (D-PA2-1):** integration is serialized, so the first unit integrates with a
  verified receipt. The second is refused with an `INTEGRATION_REJECTED` event and a blocking decision that names both units. No unit is
  integrated without a recorded check result, and none is integrated after failing one.
- **Operation schema** 4 → **5** (D-PA2-4): v4 records migrate unchanged. Older builds refuse v5, so an operation started on v1.3.0 cannot
  be resumed by a v1.2.x build that would skip the cumulative checks. Coordinate with Codex lanes on `operation_schema.ts` and its tests:
  only one bump per release window. Rebase onto theirs if they bump first, and fold this into the same version.

### Security analysis
- Merged checks run host-side, unsandboxed, in the integration worktree, as `verifyMerged` does today. Earlier units' verifier commands
  are the same commands that already ran there at their own integration, so trust does not widen. Sandboxing integration checks (reusing
  VR-1's verify sandbox) is a documented follow-up.
- A unit cannot weaken another unit's test and pass: that is the verification-file rule above.
- A unit's own `true`-style verifier cannot mask an earlier failing check, because all checks run.
- An operator verifier is never dropped on resume (union).
- The integration worktree is restored on every failure path. A failed restore blocks the operation (`blockOnGit`, `operation_runner.ts:656-668`).
- No path marks a unit VERIFIED from integration, and the turn-level outcome ladder is untouched.

## PF-3: transport beyond a parent's stdio (unix socket, token, attach and reattach)

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "a second client attaches to a running session; a wrong token is refused; the socket is mode 0600".
Unit text: "a unix domain socket (default) with a token and origin check for any localhost HTTP/WebSocket listener (reference: goose
`acp/transport/auth.rs`, constant-time compare); several clients may attach and reattach".

### What exists (read)
- `SidecarServer` (`cli/src/sidecar.ts:106`) drives one `ApplicationCore` and writes every event through one `write` callback
  (`SidecarOptions.write`, `:89-103`; `emit` → `formatSafeSidecarEvent` → `encodeEvent`, `:1362-1365`). Its state is per process, apart from
  negotiation, which is per connection: `negotiated` (`:148`), and `initialize` (`:315-331`) refuses a second `initialize` with BAD_REQUEST.
- Approvals: `requestApproval`/`openApproval` queue one at a time and emit `approval.request` with id `approval-N` (`:860-891`).
  `resolveApproval` with `always: true` sets `alwaysApprove`, switches the mode to `auto` and re-emits `session.state` (`:893-908`, grant at
  `:899-904`). So today any writer to the sidecar's stdin can grant allow-always.
- `hello` and the first `session.state` are emitted once, in `start()` (`:170-196`). `emitSessionState` is private (`:1335-1360`).
- Process entry `main` (`:1529-1625`): its own commander, the client lease, pending-restore recovery, `buildConfig`, and stdin through
  `readline` with **no line cap** (`:1615-1618`, and `docs/PROTOCOL.md` ~`:42` "sets no limit on the length of a line it reads"). EOF
  on stdin means shutdown (`:1619-1623`). Guarded by `isEntryPoint` (`:1628-1643`).
- Protocol: `PROTOCOL_VERSION=1`, range `:13-22`, `SIDECAR_CAPABILITIES` `:34-55`, `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES=[]` `:62`, `ErrorCode` `:76`,
  `SidecarCommand` `:257-288`, `parseCommand` `:305`. Schema `docs/protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json` + ledger `docs/protocol/VERSIONS.json`
  (additive changes keep protocol 1 with a note, `docs/protocol/README.md` "Recording a version decision"). `docs/PROTOCOL.md:9-15` states
  "No socket or network transport ... (planned as PF-3)".
- Reusable pieces: `BoundedLineReader` (`cli/src/acp/jsonrpc.ts:34-103`, cap and oversized reporting), `ACP_MAX_LINE_BYTES=4 MiB` and
  `ACP_MAX_OVERSIZED_LINES=3` (`acp/types.ts:97-99`), `ACP_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS=600` (`acp/types.ts:120`), and the ACP refusal of auto
  approval at startup (`index.ts:1526-1539`, `acpStartupRefusal`). The private-dir and `lstat` pattern is in `core/client_lease.ts`
  (`clientLeasePath`: `/tmp/nexus-client-leases-<uid>`, 0700, lstat-checked), and `writePrivateFile` is in `core/durable_file.ts:120`.
- Sandbox already hides `/run/user/<uid>` from write-mode bwrap commands (`--tmpfs`, `cli/src/sandbox.ts:804-806`), and `/tmp` is a
  fresh tmpfs in both bwrap branches. The read-only branch starts from `--tmpfs /` (`:741-770`). Docker mounts only the workspace.
- XERJ (goose, lexical): `crates/goose/src/acp/transport/mod.rs:184-223` uses an `x-secret-key` header with an `AcpOriginPolicy`,
  but its aux routes use `CorsLayer::allow_origin(Any)`. We take the shared-secret idea and reject any HTTP listener.

### Design
**Scope decision (D-PF3-1):** v1.3.0 ships **a unix domain socket only, with no TCP, HTTP or WebSocket listener**. The unit asks for an origin check
only "for any localhost HTTP/WebSocket listener", so with no such listener there is nothing to check. The acceptance names only the
socket, the token and mode 0600, so it is met in full. A browser cannot open an `AF_UNIX` connection, so DNS rebinding and CSRF have no
way in. A guard test keeps a port from appearing.

**Command:** `nexus serve` (new file `cli/src/serve_cli.ts`, `registerServeCommand(program)`; `index.ts` gains 2 lines beside
`registerOperationCommands`, `:1542`). It takes the global options (endpoint, model, `-w`, `--sandbox`, `--authoritative-verifier`, ...) as
`acp` does (`index.ts:1529`). Its own options are `--idle-timeout <secs>` (default 1800; 0 means never) and `--session <id>` (resume, as the
sidecar's `-r`). It refuses to start, with exit 2:
- under auto approval (`-y`, `--mode auto`, `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto`), reusing `acpStartupRefusal`;
- when commands would run unconfined (D-PF3-6): the effective sandbox profile must be `:workspace`, `:network` or `:read-only` (SB-1's
  `describeSandboxPosture`). With no `--sandbox`, `serve` defaults to `:workspace`. `--sandbox none` is refused. Before SB-1 lands, use
  `sandbox: "auto"` and refuse `none`.

Stdout prints exactly one line, `{"v":1,"type":"listening","socket":"<path>","descriptor":"<path>","pid":N,"experimental":true}`, and nothing
else; diagnostics go to stderr. The **token is never printed**.

**Runtime directory** (`socketRuntimeDir(env, uid)` in a new `cli/src/session_socket.ts`):
1. `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nexus` when `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is absolute and `lstat` shows a real directory owned by the euid with `mode & 0o077 === 0`.
2. Otherwise `/tmp/nexus-sockets-<uid>`, created 0700 and lstat-checked exactly as `clientLeasePath` does (not a symlink, owned by
   the euid, no group/other bits). Fail closed with a message naming the path.
3. The `nexus` subdir is created 0700. A pre-existing one is accepted only if it passes the same checks.

**Files per server** (`s-<16 hex>` from `randomBytes(8)`, so every path is well under the 108-byte `sun_path` limit):
- `s-<hex>.sock`: `server.listen({ path })`, then `fs.chmodSync(path, 0o600)` before the descriptor is written. The 0700 directory means no
  other uid can connect even in the window before the chmod.
- `s-<hex>.json` (`writePrivateFile`, 0600, atomic), format `nexus-socket/1`:
  `{"format":"nexus-socket/1","socket":"<abs>","token":"<64 lowercase hex>","pid":N,"session":"<session id>","workspace":"<abs>","started_at":"<ISO>","protocol_min":1,"protocol_max":1,"experimental":true}`.
  The token is 32 bytes from `crypto.randomBytes`, new for every server start.
- On exit (shutdown, SIGTERM, SIGINT, idle timeout) the socket and the descriptor are unlinked. At start, a sweep deletes `s-*.json`
  and `.sock` pairs whose `pid` is gone (`kill(pid,0)` → ESRCH) **and** whose socket refuses a connection (ECONNREFUSED). Any other state
  is left alone and logged.

**Wire format:** the same NDJSON as stdio, read with `BoundedLineReader`. The cap is 4 KiB before attach and 4 MiB
(`SOCKET_MAX_LINE_BYTES`, new in `protocol.ts`) after it. Each oversized line gets BAD_REQUEST, and the third one closes the connection.

Attach handshake: within 5 s of connecting, the first line must be:
```
{"v":1,"type":"attach","id":"<id>","token":"<64 hex>","role":"control"|"observe","client":{"name":"...","version":"..."}}
```
- Success: `{"v":1,"type":"attached","id":"<id>","connection":"c<N>","role":"control"|"observe","session":"<id>","experimental":true}`,
  then this connection alone gets the current `hello` and `session.state`. A controller also gets the pending `approval.request`, re-sent
  with the **same id**, if one is open.
- Any failure (bad, missing or short token, malformed attach, attach not first, timeout) gets one identical
  `{"type":"error","id":<id or absent>,"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"attach refused"}`, then the socket ends. The message does not say why.
  The comparison is `timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, after `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`.
- A `role: "control"` request while a controller is attached gets `BUSY` ("another client controls this session"). There is no takeover.
- Over 8 connections gets `BUSY` and close.
- `attach` sent on stdio gets BAD_REQUEST ("attach is only used on a socket connection").

Protocol additions (additive, so protocol stays 1, with a `VERSIONS.json` entry): `attach` in `SidecarCommand`; `attached` in
`SidecarEvent`; `ErrorCode += "UNAUTHORIZED" | "NOT_CONTROLLER" | "NOT_PERMITTED"`; the constant `SOCKET_MAX_LINE_BYTES`. The Rust TUI
does not use the socket. Its event parser ignores unknown event types, so the Rust change is limited to regenerating the samples
(`cli/test/fixtures/protocol_v1_schema_samples.jsonl`).

**Multi-client model (hub = `SessionSocketServer` in `session_socket.ts`):** one `SidecarServer` per `nexus serve` process. Its `write`
**broadcasts** each already-formatted line to every attached connection; no ids are rewritten.
- **Controller** (at most one): may send `prompt.submit`, `steer`, `cancel`, `approve` (once only), `deny`, `answer`, `checkpoint.choice`,
  `receipt`, `tool.detail`, `models.list`, `model.select`, `shutdown`, and `slash` where `readOnlySlashAllowed(command,args)` (`sidecar.ts:38-49`)
  holds and the command is not `mode auto`, plus `slash compact`.
- **Not permitted over the socket** (`NOT_PERMITTED`, sent to the sender only, nothing forwarded): `approve` with `always:true`, which the hub
  downgrades to `always:false` and answers with a `notice` to the controller: "allow-always is not available over the socket; approved once".
  Also refused: `slash mode auto`, `!<cmd>`, `/cd`, any other slash outside the allowlist, and `provider.connect|cancel|local-cancel|disconnect`.
  Rule: **a socket client can drive turns and give one human yes or no per approval. It cannot raise the session's authority or change
  Nexus configuration** (D-PF3-4).
- **Observer:** may send only `initialize` and nothing else (`NOT_CONTROLLER` to that observer only). It sees the full stream, including
  `approval.request` and responses to the controller's requests.
- `initialize` is answered **by the hub, per connection**, through a pure `negotiate(clientMin, clientMax, experimental, offered)` extracted
  from `SidecarServer.initialize` (`:315-331`; behaviour-preserving, and `SidecarServer.initialize` calls it). It is never forwarded, so the
  server's `negotiated` stays unset. `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES` is empty today, so experimental sidecar features are simply unavailable over the socket.
- **Reattach:** when the controller disconnects, a pending approval **stays pending** and the turn keeps running. The next connection that
  attaches as `control` receives the re-sent `approval.request` and may answer it. An approval with no controller attached for 600 s
  (`ACP_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS`) is **denied** (`resolveApproval(id,false,false)`, which never grants), with a notice. There is no replay of
  events from before an attach (D-PF3-8): an attacher gets current state, and can fetch `receipt` afterwards.
- **Lifecycle:** the server exits on the controller's `shutdown`, on SIGTERM or SIGINT, or on idle timeout. Idle means zero connections
  and no turn running for `--idle-timeout`. EOF from one client is a detach and never a shutdown.
- **Backpressure:** a connection whose `socket.writableLength` exceeds 8 MiB is destroyed (logged on stderr). A slow observer cannot stall
  the session or other clients.

`SidecarServer` changes (small, behaviour-preserving for stdio):
- `public helloEvent()` and `public sessionStateEvent()`, extracted from `start()` and `emitSessionState()`.
- `public pendingApprovalEvent(): SidecarEvent | undefined`: `openApproval` keeps the event object it emitted on `pendingApproval`.
- `public answerApprovalForTimeout(id)`, or reuse `resolveApproval(id,false,false)` through a public `deny(id)`.
- `negotiate()` extracted.
None of these runs in the stdio path differently. The wire recordings (`cli/test/fixtures/wire/*.json`, `protocol_wire.test.ts`) must replay
unchanged.

**Library side** (with PF-4): `attachSidecar({ descriptor | socket+token, role })` in `cli/src/sidecar_client.ts` returns the same
`SidecarClient` over a `net.Socket`. It reads the descriptor itself (`lstat` + regular file + 0600 + owner = euid, ≤ 4 KiB).

### Security analysis
- **Who can connect:** only processes with the same uid (and root). The 0700 directory plus the 0600 socket means `connect()` needs search
  permission on the directory and write permission on the socket. Node cannot read `SO_PEERCRED` without a native addon, so peer uid is not
  checked; that is documented.
- **What the token protects against:** (1) a process that can reach the socket path but cannot read the descriptor (a sandbox that
  bind-mounts a path, or a widened directory mode); (2) attaching to the wrong server when a path or descriptor is stale or mixed up;
  (3) accidental attach by same-uid tools that walk sockets. **It does not protect against unconfined code running as the user**, which can
  read the descriptor. That is why `serve` requires confined commands (D-PF3-6): a model-driven `run_command` in bwrap sees a tmpfs at
  `/run/user/<uid>` and `/tmp`. Slice 2 adds an explicit `--tmpfs <socket dir>` to both bwrap branches and the worker wrap, so a
  non-standard `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is masked too. Docker never mounts it. Residual hole, documented: unsandboxed MCP servers and plugins, and
  any host process of the user, can read the token and attach as observer, or as controller when none is attached.
- **A second client cannot answer the first client's approval:** only the single controller connection may approve or deny. An observer gets
  `NOT_CONTROLLER` and the approval stays pending. The answer comes from a human through a client, and the gate decided first
  (`docs/PROTOCOL.md:17`). A forged `approve` for a refused action cannot reach a gate the sidecar already refused, because no
  `approval.request` exists for it (`NO_PENDING_APPROVAL`).
- **No grant over the socket:** no allow-always, no `/mode auto`, no `!` shell, no `/cd`, and no credential writes. Managed policy is
  unchanged: the sidecar config was clamped at `buildConfig`.
- **DoS bounds:** at most 8 connections, a 4 KiB pre-auth line, a 5 s attach deadline, 4 MiB lines, three oversized lines then close, and
  8 MiB of outbound buffer per connection.
- The token never appears in logs, stdout, events, errors or the flight log. `formatSafeSidecarEvent` never sees commands.

### Files
Add: `cli/src/session_socket.ts` (runtime dir, descriptor, hub, token compare); `cli/src/serve_cli.ts`;
`cli/test/session_socket.test.ts`; `cli/test/serve_cli.test.ts`; `examples/attach/attach.mjs` + `README.md`; `docs/SOCKET_TRANSPORT.md`.
Change: `cli/src/sidecar.ts` (event builders, `negotiate`, reject `attach` on stdio); `cli/src/protocol.ts` (types and codes); regenerated
`docs/protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json`, `docs/protocol/VERSIONS.json`, `cli/test/fixtures/protocol_v1_schema_samples.jsonl`;
`cli/src/index.ts` (+2 lines); `cli/src/sandbox.ts` (socket-dir mask); `cli/src/sidecar_client.ts` (`attachSidecar`);
`docs/PROTOCOL.md` (transport section, remove the ":13 no socket" line, error codes); `examples/README.md`; `cli/test/examples.test.ts`.

2. `a wrong token is refused with UNAUTHORIZED, nothing else is sent, and the server keeps serving` (acceptance). Hostile variants: missing,

## PF-4: library entry point

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "an example script runs a verified task through the entry point in CI". Unit text: "a `lib` entry that does not
run commander on import, `exports` and `types` in `cli/package.json`, a package name decision, a documented minimal embedding example that
spawns the sidecar".

### What exists

  `exports`, `types` or `private`.
- `cli/tsconfig.json`: no `declaration`.
- `cli/src/index.ts` is the CLI. Importing it runs top-level code: `isolateEvalCommandHome`, the client lease, restore recovery,
  `loadEnvironment()` and possible `process.exit(2)` (`:70-134`), then `await program.parseAsync(process.argv)` (`:1565`). It re-exports
  `ApplicationCore` after that (`:1567-1568`, the "accidental re-export" of PLAN §2). The managed-policy startup check is in the `preAction`
  hook (`:1545-1563`).
- The sidecar is a process: `cli/src/sidecar.ts` `main`, guarded by `isEntryPoint` (`:1628-1643`). The CLI finds it with
  `resolveSidecarScript` (`index.ts:193-213`) and the TUI is launched with `--sidecar <script> --node <execPath>` (`:215-227`).

  pending-restore recovery and `requireManagedPolicyAtStartup`, all of which `sidecar.ts main` (`:1589-1601`) and `index.ts` perform.

  → `turn.outcome === "VERIFIED"`). `examples/verified-completion/` does the same through the CLI.

  `npm ci --omit=dev`. The CI repro job builds twice and `cmp`s the tarball, sums, notices, SBOM and installer (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:327-334`,
  `release.yml:109-116`). `scripts/smoke-package.sh` smoke-tests the extracted tarball. CI builds `cli` before tests (`ci.yml:153-154`).
- No repository code resolves the package by name (`git grep local-code-harness` finds only an evidence doc).

  (`BoundedLineReader`) and node builtins. Everything else is `export type`.

  export { spawnSidecar, SidecarClient, SidecarClientError } from "./sidecar_client.js";
  export type { SpawnSidecarOptions, PromptOptions, ApprovalHandler, ApprovalDecision } from "./sidecar_client.js";
  export type { SidecarEvent, SidecarCommand, ErrorCode } from "./protocol.js";
  export type { TurnResult, EngineeringOutcome, ExecutionState } from "./core/turn.js";

### Design
- **Selection syntax (D-SB1-1):** no new flag and no new env setting. The existing `--sandbox [mode]` (global, `index.ts:394`, and
  sidecar `:1554`) also accepts a profile:
  `^(auto|bwrap|docker)?(:workspace|:read-only|:network)?$` (at least one part; case-sensitive; ≤ 32 chars), plus the legacy `none`.
  Examples: `--sandbox :workspace`, `--sandbox bwrap:network`. Legacy values keep their exact meaning and set **no** explicit profile.
  Anything else exits 2 listing the valid values. It never falls back to unconfined.
- **New pure module `cli/src/sandbox_profile.ts`:**
  ```ts
  export const SANDBOX_PROFILE_NAMES = [":workspace", ":read-only", ":network"] as const;
  export type SandboxProfileName = typeof SANDBOX_PROFILE_NAMES[number];
  export type ProfileLabel = SandboxProfileName | "unconfined";
  export function parseSandboxValue(raw: string | true | undefined): { engine?: "auto"|"bwrap"|"docker"|"none"; profile?: SandboxProfileName } // throws SandboxProfileError
  export const PROFILE_SPECS: Record<SandboxProfileName, { readOnly: boolean; network: boolean; summary: string; residual: readonly string[] }>;
  export interface SandboxPosture { profile: ProfileLabel; explicit: boolean; engine: "auto"|"bwrap"|"docker"|"none"; network: boolean; readOnly: boolean; source: string; residual: string[] }
  export function describeSandboxPosture(i: { sandbox: boolean|string|undefined; readOnly: boolean; network: boolean; profile?: SandboxProfileName; source?: string }): SandboxPosture
  export function profileRank(p: ProfileLabel): 0|1|2|3; // unconfined < :network < :workspace < :read-only
  ```
- **Mapping (profiles only rename and bundle existing confinement):**

  | Profile | Equals today's flags | Engine | Workspace | HOME | Network |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `:workspace` | `--sandbox [engine]` (default auto), network forced off | bwrap, else docker | rw | tmpfs + toolchain ro mounts | off, even when `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK=1` (warnOnce) |
  | `:network` | `--sandbox [engine] --sandbox-network` | same | rw | same | on |
  | `:read-only` | `--read-only` (`docker:read-only` is refused: read-only confinement is bwrap-only, `tools.ts:1722`) | bwrap | ro (fd-pinned) | tmpfs | off |
  | (none set) | today's behaviour unchanged; the label is derived: readOnly → `:read-only`; sandbox on and network → `:network`; sandbox on → `:workspace`; otherwise `unconfined` | | | | |
- **Composition:**
  - `:read-only` sets `readOnly`, which wins over `--yes`/`--mode auto` exactly as `--read-only` does (`config.ts:466-469`). A tightening.
  - `:workspace` and `:network` leave the approval mode untouched.
  - `--sandbox-network` with `:workspace` or `:read-only` → exit 2 (explicit conflict). With `:network` it is redundant and accepted.
  - Managed policy: `:network` under `sandbox.forbid_network` is refused through `clampSandboxNetwork(policy, true, "--sandbox :network")`.
  - `sandbox.required` with no profile raises the derived label to `:workspace`/`:network` with the policy source (already
    `clampSandbox`).
  - **No new managed policy key** (D-SB1-2): the floor is expressed by the existing keys. A `sandbox.min_profile` key is deferred (it
    would bump the policy `schema_version` while GV-1/GV-5 finish).
- **Network truth:** `sandbox_network.ts` gains `setSandboxNetworkProfile(v: boolean|undefined)`. `sandboxNetworkEnabled()` returns the
  profile value first when set (`sandbox.ts:198`). This closes "the sandbox does not consult the policy" for profiled sessions, because the env
  variable can no longer re-enable network at call time.
- **Config:** `HarnessConfig.sandboxProfile?: SandboxProfileName` (`types.ts`, set only when explicit) and `config.sandbox` as the engine.
- **Visibility:**
  - One describer replaces the three copies (`sidecar.ts:1340`, `doctor.ts:1361`, `repl.ts:380`).
  - `session.state.posture` gains `profile?: string` (additive; schema regen, `VERSIONS.json` entry, samples). Rust `PostureInfo` gains
    `profile: Option<String>`, shown in the TUI posture line.
  - REPL `/status`: `mode: review · sandbox: :workspace (bwrap, network off, explicit) · workspace: trusted`.
  - Doctor: `posture.profile` and `posture.profileSource` (additive; `DOCTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 2, D-SB1-4, because
    `smoke-package.sh` pins 2). The text header prints the same; `sandbox.confinement` evidence adds the profile and its residual list.
  - VR-3: `dispatch_tool_call.ts:677` metadata gains `sandboxProfile: this.sandboxPostureLabel` (one object property, no operator, so the
    complexity is unchanged; the checker confirms it), and `spine.ts:652` passes `profile`.
- **Residual holes**, documented beside each profile in `docs/SANDBOX_PROFILES.md` and in `PROFILE_SPECS.residual`:
  - broad host reads (`/` is bound read-only: `/etc`, `/usr`, other world-readable files);
  - the writable workspace includes `.git` (hooks, config) and ignored trees (`node_modules`), which later host-side tools may execute;
  - toolchain directories are readable;
  - no seccomp filter under bwrap;
  - `:network` is unrestricted egress (no domain filter, separate from the egress inspector);
  - MCP servers and plugins are not sandboxed;
  - the worker falls back to unconfined under `auto` when no engine exists for the **worker**, while commands still refuse
    (`tools.ts:789-831`);
  - `nexus verify --sandbox` does not accept profiles (D-SB1-5).

### Security analysis
A profile is a name for an existing flag bundle and cannot grant:
- No code path reads `sandboxProfile` to decide approval, full access, verification-path mode, CS-9 rules or managed policy.
- `:read-only` only tightens.
- Parsing is strict and fails closed.
- Network can only be turned on by the explicit `:network`, which managed policy can refuse.
- Profile strings never reach a shell: they are parsed against an enum.

G-3 cases below.

## PA-2: verified merge arbitration

**Acceptance (verbatim):** "two units whose changes conflict semantically (each passes alone) fail verification on the merged tree and
neither is integrated silently". Unit text: "when parallel units integrate, apply each diff, run verification on the merged tree, reject
on failure".

### Definitions, from the code
- **Unit:** a `WorkUnit` of a durable operation (`nexus operation run`, `/batch`, `/team`) whose operation has `git.isolate: true`. Only
  then may `maxConcurrentUnits > 1` (`core/operation_schema.ts:~301`; `docs/v1.3.0/PA1_RESOURCE_ADMISSION.md`; `docs/v1.3.0/BATCH.md`).
  Each unit runs in its own worktree and branch from the integration tip (`core/operation_git.ts:1-11`). `/loop` and `/goal` are single
  workspace drivers and produce no merge (`loop.ts`, `goal.ts`), so they are outside PA-2.
- **Merge:** `OperationGit.integrate` (`operation_git.ts:274-428`): commit the unit's worktree; `git merge --no-ff --no-verify` the unit
  branch into `nexus/op-<key>/integration` in the integration worktree (`:388-397`); on a textual conflict, abort and return `conflict`
  (`:392-397`). Integration is **serialized** by `OperationRunner.enqueueIntegration` (`core/operation_runner.ts:485-506`).
  `integrateUnit` (`:512-580`) turns `conflict` and `failed` into operator decisions (`MERGE_CONFLICT`, `INTEGRATION_FAILED`) and
  `integrated` into a receipt (`IntegrationReceipt`, `core/operation.ts:351-367`) plus `WORK_INTEGRATED`.
- **Verification on the merged tree today:** `verifyMerged(command)` (`operation_git.ts:627-646`, `runVerifierShell` in the integration
  worktree) re-runs **only the integrating unit's own verifier**, and only if that verifier PASSED with executed tests (`:400-402`). A
  failure resets the merge (`:404-409`, `restoreIntegration`). Without a verifier the receipt says `NOT_RUN` and the unit is integrated
  "(not re-verified)" (`operation_runner.ts:565-571`). The crash path re-checks after the fact (`:345-379`). Existing test:
  `cli/test/operation_git.test.ts:170-194`.
- **The gap that fails the acceptance:** with units A and B, B integrated first and passing, then A merging cleanly, A's own narrow verifier
  passes on the merged tree, **B's verifier is never re-run**, and A is integrated even though B's tests now fail. That is the silent
  semantic conflict.

### Design
- **Merged-tree check set** (`integrationChecks()` in `operation_git.ts`), ordered and de-duplicated by exact command string, with owners
  merged:
  1. the operator's verifiers pinned for the operation: `OperationGitState.integrationVerifiers?: string[]`, set at the first run from
     `config.authoritativeVerifierCommand` and unioned with the current one on resume (tighten-only);
  2. the integrating unit's own verifier (as today: PASSED with executed tests);
  3. every earlier receipt's `tests.command` with `status === "PASSED" && hasExecutedTests`, in `sequence` order.

  At most **16** distinct commands (D-PA2-3). Beyond that the integration is `failed` ("too many distinct verifiers; give the operation an
  `--authoritative-verifier`").
- **Run:** sequentially on the merged tip in the integration worktree with the existing per-command timeout; stop at the first failure.
- **Attribution:** on failure, `restoreIntegration(tip)` (as today), then re-run **only the failing check** on the pre-merge tip.
  - It passes there → **semantic conflict**: `failed` with reason "merging <A> breaks the verifier of <owners> (`cmd`) on the merged tree;
    it passes without <A>", `conflictWith: owners`.
  - It fails there too → "the integration branch already fails `cmd` before <A> was merged (environment or unstable verifier); not
    attributed to <A>".
  - Exit 126/127 keeps today's environment message.
- **Verification-file takeover (hostile):** if the merge diff (`tip..mergedTip`) modifies a path that is (a) in an earlier receipt's
  `files` and (b) a verification path by `SecurityManager`'s classifier (`security.ts`, `VERIFICATION_CONFIG_PROTECTED` and the
  verification-path patterns), the merge is reset and `failed` with "<A> changes verification files integrated by <B>: …", before any
  check runs. Without this, A could weaken B's test and pass B's check.
- **Shapes (additive):**
  `interface MergedCheck { command: string; owners: string[] /* unit ids or "operator" */; status: "PASSED"|"FAILED"|"ENVIRONMENT"|"TIMED_OUT"; baseline?: "PASSED"|"FAILED" }`.
  `IntegrationReceipt.mergedChecks?: MergedCheck[]`. `IntegrateResult` `failed` gains `checks?: MergedCheck[]; conflictWith?: string[]`.
  New `OperationEventType` `"INTEGRATION_REJECTED"` with `detail: { unitId, conflictWith, checks }`. Block cause stays
  `INTEGRATION_FAILED`. The question names both units, with options `retry` (re-run the unit with the reason) and `revise`. The existing
  `verification` field values keep their meaning.
- **Crash path** (`:345-379`): uses the same set, and keeps today's "merge already in place" handling on failure.
- **Empty set** (no operator verifier, no unit verifier, no earlier verifiers): `NOT_RUN`, as today, with the same event. This is not
  silent, because the receipt and the event say "not re-verified".
- **Interpretation of "neither is integrated silently" (D-PA2-1):** integration is serialized, so the first unit integrates with a
  verified receipt. The second is refused with an `INTEGRATION_REJECTED` event and a blocking decision that names both units. No unit is
  integrated without a recorded check result, and none is integrated after failing one.
- **Operation schema** 4 → **5** (D-PA2-4): v4 records migrate unchanged. Older builds refuse v5, so an operation started on v1.3.0 cannot
  be resumed by a v1.2.x build that would skip the cumulative checks. Coordinate with Codex lanes on `operation_schema.ts` and its tests:
  only one bump per release window. Rebase onto theirs if they bump first, and fold this into the same version.

### Security analysis
- Merged checks run host-side, unsandboxed, in the integration worktree, as `verifyMerged` does today. Earlier units' verifier commands
  are the same commands that already ran there at their own integration, so trust does not widen. Sandboxing integration checks (reusing
  VR-1's verify sandbox) is a documented follow-up.
- A unit cannot weaken another unit's test and pass: that is the verification-file rule above.
- A unit's own `true`-style verifier cannot mask an earlier failing check, because all checks run.
- An operator verifier is never dropped on resume (union).
- The integration worktree is restored on every failure path. A failed restore blocks the operation (`blockOnGit`, `operation_runner.ts:656-668`).
- No path marks a unit VERIFIED from integration, and the turn-level outcome ladder is untouched.

# graphify
`/graphify` → invoke the Skill tool with `skill: "graphify"` (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) before anything else.

# RTK (Rust Token Killer)

A hook rewrites shell commands through `rtk` (60-90% fewer tokens): write ordinary commands (`git status` runs as `rtk git status`).

- Raw output: `rtk proxy <cmd>`. Use it to debug, and whenever a rewritten `grep`, `awk` or `sed` pipeline returns filtered or odd output; rerun it raw before trusting it.
- Savings: `rtk gain`, `rtk gain --history`. Missed opportunities: `rtk discover`.
- If `rtk gain` fails, a different `rtk` is installed (reachingforthejack/rtk, Rust Type Kit); check `which rtk`.

## Principles

1. Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.
2. Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.
3. Touch only what you must. Clean up only your mess.
4. Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

## Agent workflow

Specialised agents live in `~/.claude/agents/` (their descriptions are in the agent list). Delegate any feature, bug fix or significant change to **`@orchestrator`**: it runs the pipeline and returns one structured summary (changes, test results, review findings, issues) while the verbose output stays in its context.

Call a single agent directly for one stage: architect, coder, tester, reviewer, design-qa, security-auditor, migration-planner (alembic, sqlite3), api-designer, ci-validator (GitLab CI).

Handle these yourself, without delegating: codebase questions, reading and explaining code, git operations, deployments, config changes.

| aisyndicate | Next.js 16, React, TypeScript, Radix UI | `./aisyndicate/` |

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. # Work state: your to-do lists and working state

Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown at the start of every session in this project.

- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)

REA provides reverse-engineering tools for local artifacts, native binaries, managed code, browser pages, and runtimes. Use the tool that directly answers the question; discover targets or inspect inventory only when needed. Tool results include inline Evidence and report their coverage and limitations. An opened target persists across turns. When finished, export needed Evidence and call close_binary; its snapshot_path can retain analysis.
